ny_sunset_wall.blurb: Sunset Wall is a short sport section on the Horseshoe North Cliff at Thacher Park, in the Helderberg escarpment west of Albany. Its eleven bolted routes are on limestone, and the grades are friendly: one easy 5.5, then a solid core of 5.8 to 5.10 with a single 5.11 at the top end. That makes it a good place for climbers stepping up from the low grades or looking for a few moderates in one spot. The face picks up sun through the afternoon and into the evening, so it suits cooler days and late sessions. The climbers' trail follows the cliff base around the bend of the horseshoe, then a short uphill stretch leads to the routes, some via spur paths.

ny_teepee_wall.blurb: TeePee Wall is a small cliff on Crane Mountain, a quiet Adirondack foothill near Warrensburg where the crags are scattered across the mountainside and see few climbers. The wall sits beside the trail up to Black Arches Wall, and the lower part is clean and steep. Ten of the eleven routes are traditional leads and one is a top-rope, ranging from an easy 5.6 through the 5.8 to 5.10 band up to a single hard 5.11. It is a spot for a short day of crack and face climbing with gear, and expect a real hike in, since the walk to the base is roughly half an hour or more. Rock around Crane tends to be solid but a bit dirty.

ny_jewels_and_gems.blurb: Jewels and Gems is a small roadside crag beside NY 73 in Chapel Pond Pass, in the Adirondacks. The rock is anorthosite, and the cliff is about 60 to 70 feet tall and mostly in shade, which keeps it comfortable in summer. Of its eleven routes, ten are trad and one is a top-rope; grades start at the very easy end and run mostly through 5.6 to 5.9, with a few at 5.10 and 5.11. Anchors are reachable from above, so top-roping is common. The approach takes about a minute from the pull-off shared with the King Wall, though the cliff is hard to spot from the road. It can be busy on weekends, but parties tend not to stay long.
